correctness.rationale: For any real payoffs and positive aspiration normalizers at positive temperature, clearing strictly positive logistic denominators gives an exponential polynomial with three affine coefficient blocks, hence at most five real zeros counted with multiplicity by a self-contained induction using Rolle. The drift points inward at both endpoints, giving at most three attracting zeros. For the symmetric game the reflection identity, strict pointwise monotonicity in inverse temperature below x=1/3, continuity and divergent crossing curve at both endpoints establish a positive attained critical inverse temperature. The zero bound forces exact 1/3/5 root counts and multiplicities; strict inverse-temperature derivative and second x derivative make the folds nondegenerate. The central root is hyperbolic for all temperatures by 1+exp(z)>3z. Strict Taylor inequalities prove five distinct roots at inverse temperature L=3. The shipped standard-library program replays exact sign inequalities and finite diagnostics but does not replace the analytical global proof.

originality.rationale: The source already shows five observed fixed points, two fold events and theta about 0.18; these are explicitly not claimed as new. The precise contribution is the parameter-uniform sharp capacity and the analytical all-temperature uniqueness/exhaustiveness of the exact symmetric fold, including multiplicities and global basins. Classical extended-Chebyshev theory covers the exponential-polynomial zero-count principle, but does not by itself establish the model-constrained sharpness nor the unique critical-temperature classification. The 2025 companion concerns networked aspiration and the 2022 predecessor uses imitation updating; neither inspected material logically dominates the full claim. Actual semantic record and primary-literature searches found no direct stronger theorem; publication priority remains uncertain.
residual_risks: Published primary source already reports both fold transitions numerically, so novelty is limited to mathematical exactness, uniqueness, and model-wide sharp bounds.
Extended-Chebyshev theory covers the generic real-zero-count lemma; priority is claimed only for the full game-specific phase theorem, not its constituent classical technique.
The wider aspiration and logistic evolutionary-game literature is large; a directly covering earlier proof could have escaped the searches.
The companion paper was only inspected in material relevant to equivalent mechanisms and global conclusions; no claim that every line of its full text was independently audited.

value.rationale: The maximum number of attracting cooperation outcomes is a natural model capacity, and the complete one-versus-three attractor phase boundary upgrades a published numerical multistability collapse to an exact and exhaustive bifurcation theorem. Uniqueness of the threshold and nondegenerate fold structure make the critical noise level mathematically well defined and give all initial-condition basins; the theorem is not merely a textbook root bound or an arbitrary numerical slice. Its scope is scientifically motivated by source Section IV and by the coexistence/multistability question.
